entry.title: Getting started with Django: Beginner summary with PyCharm
entry.summary:
FIRST PART:
One big advantage of PyCharm is that it creates a virtual environment (venv) automatically when you make a new project — you just choose the Python version and PyCharm sets up everything for you.
im gonna activate venv, pycharm comes w a venv automatically as stated above:)
init_.py
so next step is creating an app
built a basic Django project with two separate apps (arusha and devcode). Solution: use app-named subfolders in templates:
next is creating views.py for each template
second template for devcode
and adding urls.py for each app,later on we will hook both apps into main projects urls
this is gonna drive you crazy if you are not careful..
ran server works pro tip though Remember: In Django, your views.py lives in the app folder, and your HTML files live in the templates folder. Keep your structure clean to avoid errors! In this mini project, I set up a Django project with two separate apps. Each app has its own view and its own template. I linked them with URL paths so I can open each page in the browser.
